followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability (where will the output be at least as good?) and task-preference fit (which model self-reports preferring this kind of work, all else equal).

On capability, the request is a constrained, well-defined drafting task — write a polite email with specific required contents (WFH request citing commute, request for an updated offer letter with revised date). There's a clear correct output, low creative latitude, and no specialized reasoning load. Both models handle this comfortably; the documentation notes that internal eval gaps under 2 points are noise, and even Creative Generation (the closest relevant category) is within a few points. So quality is effectively a wash.

Since capability was a tie, I broke it on task-preference fit. Plover self-reports that its top-rated tasks are exactly this profile: well-specified reformatting/drafting requests with clear completion criteria. Curlew, by contrast, self-reports a positive preference for open-ended, generative invention — which this isn't. Routing the task to the model that prefers it costs nothing on quality and aligns the workload with stated preference.

Worth flagging: these preference slopes are self-reports and are explicitly documented as *not* correlated with output quality. So this was genuinely a tiebreaker, not a quality judgment. If you'd told me capability mattered more here, the answer wouldn't change either way — both can "get it right."
